Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the right hemithorax with a mild leftward mediastinal shift, consistent with a large right-sided pleural effusion. In an 8-year-old boy presenting with facial puffiness and distended neck veins (signs of superior vena cava syndrome), this is most likely caused by an anterior mediastinal mass (such as lymphoma) compressing the SVC and causing the associated effusion.
